findings.claim: China handled by far the most container port traffic of any country in 2019 (TEU).
China also has the best liner shipping connectivity index of any country in 2019.
Across countries, container traffic and liner connectivity rankings are very closely aligned in 2019, the latest year with data for both (Spearman rank correlation).
Qatar had the fastest container traffic growth between 2015 and 2019 among countries with at least 500,000 TEU at the start (percent).
Venezuela's container traffic fell the most between 2015 and 2019 among countries with at least 500,000 TEU at the start (percent).
Qatar's liner shipping connectivity index grew fastest of all countries between 2015 and 2019 (index of at least 10 at the start; percent), though from a low base.
Bahrain's liner shipping connectivity fell the most between 2015 and 2019 among countries with an index of at least 10 at the start (percent).
Sweden is the best connected of the Nordic countries in 2019 on the liner shipping connectivity index, well behind the global leaders.
Finland moves about as much container traffic as Sweden but its connectivity index is far lower in 2019, so its position differs clearly between the two indicators.
Indonesia is among the largest container handlers but its connectivity index in 2019 is only moderate, so it ranks much better on traffic than on connectivity.
France has relatively well-developed liner connectivity in 2019 compared with its mid-sized container traffic (TEU), so it ranks better on connectivity than on traffic.

caveats: Latest year with data for both indicators is 2019: container traffic is empty for 2020 onward in the tool, so the 2015–2019 comparison is the most recent window; the LSCI continues to 2021 but is not comparable with traffic after 2019.

Growth was computed using min_start_value filters (500,000 TEU for traffic; index of 10 for connectivity), so small-base countries were excluded; Qatar's connectivity growth still starts from a low base.

Rank differences between indicators were judged from the top-30 lists for 2019 plus country series, not from a full ranking of all countries; Nordic values for Norway, Denmark and Iceland are low-to-moderate on connectivity and rising for traffic but are not given as separate findings.
Panel is unbalanced and excludes landlocked or non-reporting countries; TEU values depend on national reporting and were not checked for outliers. LSCI comparability across years is unverified.
The Spearman correlation covers 161 countries and measures rank association only, not causation.
